id="S:1"><div class="content-body"><p>Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States.</p><p>The Harlequins back-rower will remain in the United Kingdom with her partner and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan due to give birth.</p><p>England face Canada on 17 and 24 October (both 00:00 BST starts) before playing the USA in one-off match on 30 October (21:15 BST).</p><p>England are boosted by the return of Kelsey Clifford for the North American tour, with the Saracens prop returning from a hamstring injury.</p><p>The Red Roses continue a tough run of fixtures after playing three matches in September, beating Australia and New Zealand but ending their record-breaking winning streak with a draw against Canada.</p><p>England head coach John Mitchell described their home Tests with Canada and the Black Ferns as "humdingers that could have gone either way."</p><p>The Tests against Canada in Toronto and Ottawa are being viewed by England as the culmination of a self-titled three-Test series.</p><p>Mitchell described his expectations for the squad: "The 32 players travelling to North America have a great opportunity to elevate our connections as a squad because playing away from home requires togetherness.</p><p>"We have shown a real hunger to compete and improve, and we're excited to rip into our preparations and continue our rivalry with Canada in Toronto."</p><p>England also confirmed that Delaney Burns, Haidee Head and Sophie McQueen would not travel due to injury.</p><p>Harlequins back rower Packer is England's most capped active player with 119 caps.</p><h2 class="heading">England squad for North America tour</h2><p><strong>Forwards:</strong>
